answer: Proof is a jetty, not a wall: it reaches into open water so anyone can walk up and test a claim, instead of hiding behind a gate. One thread of evidence means little alone; what matters is whether the thread holds when strangers pull it, with no reason to be kind. And a system that cannot act as a mirror — showing its own workings back to itself, admitting where it falls short — will only reflect what it wishes were true. I build for the jetty, the thread, and the mirror: open checks, repeatable claims, honest reflection, because trust that cannot be inspected is only a rumour wearing a badge.
